fieldMarks: Smooth olive-green to brown or dark brown back, often with blotches and sometimes yellow flecks along the sides.
Swollen parotoid glands behind each eye, unusual among ambystomatids.
Glandular ridge along the top of the tail, which tapers sharply toward the tip.
Terrestrial adults about 14-22 cm total length; aquatic adults reach about 26 cm.
Breeding males are darker than females; unmetamorphosed males have enlarged hind limbs and feet.
behavior: Non-paedomorphic adults live underground most of the year and are seen mainly at breeding time and on fall rains.
Adults migrate on rainy nights between nonbreeding habitat and breeding ponds; breeding runs from January in the south to July in the north or at elevation.
Nocturnal on land; aquatic forms are strictly nocturnal where fish are present. When alarmed it assumes a defensive posture and secretes a milky toxic substance.
Feeds on soft-bodied invertebrates such as worms, snails and insect larvae; introduced trout reduce larval survival.
habitat: Humid forest, woodland and open grassland near breeding ponds; adults shelter under rotting logs, leaf litter and debris along stream banks or in animal burrows.
Eggs are laid attached to vegetation in ponds, lakes and slow streams; montane populations are often paedomorphic (remain gilled).
range: Pacific coast from extreme southeastern Alaska through coastal British Columbia, Washington and Oregon to northern California (Mendocino area), from sea level to about 3,110 m.
